strict/padded-payload: jose accepts `=` padding on a segment; RFC 7515 §2 defines the JOSE encoding as the unpadded form, and a byte string with two spellings gives one token two texts. packages/jwt refuses.
strict/duplicate-alg: jose reads the header with JSON.parse, which keeps the LAST of two same-named members; packages/jwt refuses a header that names one twice, because the two readers need not keep the same one.
strict/duplicate-exp: As strict/duplicate-alg, on the claims set. jose accepts and reads the last `exp`; packages/jwt refuses.
strict/short-hmac-secret: jose accepts an HMAC secret shorter than the digest; RFC 7518 §3.2 requires at least the digest length, so packages/jwt refuses the key at import.
jwk/marked-for-encryption: jose ignores `use` on import; packages/jwt refuses `use: "enc"` for a signature key.
claims/numericdate/fractional-exp: jose compares a fractional `exp` numerically; RFC 7519 §2 defines a NumericDate as a whole number of seconds, so packages/jwt refuses rather than choosing a rounding direction.
claims/numericdate/huge-exp: jose compares an `exp` past 2^53 as the Float it rounded to; packages/jwt refuses, because the value that came back is not the value that was written.
